dedupe_keys.name: institute for disease modeling frameworks starsim laser and emod agent based epidemic models

description: The Institute for Disease Modeling (IDM), part of the Gates Foundation's Global Health Division, publishes three open-source frameworks for simulating the spread and control of infectious diseases. Starsim models individuals with within-host biology, co-infection and fine-grained interventions, suited to HIV, TB, sexually transmitted infections, HPV and family planning. LASER (Light Agent Spatial modeling for ERadication) models spatial spread and metapopulations with human movement, suited to large campaigns such as polio eradication and vaccination evaluation. EMOD (Epidemiological MODeling software), IDM's longest-running framework, combines individual behaviour with regional context and is most developed for malaria, including mosquito life cycles, climate and vector control. Coverage: generic frameworks applied by IDM and partners mainly in low- and middle-income countries. Format and access: Python packages (Starsim, LASER) and a C++ engine with Python tooling (EMOD) on GitHub, with documentation hubs; free. Licence: IDM states all its software is free and open source; the licence is set per repository. Caveats: models need careful calibration to local surveillance data, and the three frameworks differ in inputs and outputs, so results are not directly interchangeable. Simulation uses: agent-based projections of epidemic burden and intervention effects that inform healthcare capacity planning and emergency response for pandemics. Related records: Covasim (model-covasim), IDM's COVID-19 model from which Starsim grew, is recorded separately.
